message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI (Air Quality Index) for Los Angeles at this moment.  

If you’d like up‑to‑date information, you can check one of the following:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow.gov** | Real‑time AQI values for cities across the U.S., including Los Angeles. | Go to the website, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI and pollutant breakdown. |
| **EPA’s Air Quality Dashboard** | Historical and current AQI trends, maps, and health advisories. | Search for Los Angeles or use the interactive map. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily AQI summaries and alerts. | Look for “air quality” or “AQI” in the weather section. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., AQICN, Plume Labs) | Push notifications for AQI changes and health recommendations. | Download the app, enable location services, and receive real‑time updates. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, remember that the AQI categories are:

- **0–50** – Good  
- **51–100** – Moderate  
- **101–150** – Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  
- **151–200** – Unhealthy  
- **201–300** – Very Unhealthy  
- **301+** – Hazardous  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more details on interpreting AQI values or tips for staying healthy when the air isn’t great!
